_: THE PRICE LIST. Every number a customer pays lives in this file and nowhere else.
Not in a constant, not in a values file, not in a service. A price in code is a price that
needs a deploy to change, and a price that needs a deploy is one nobody changes — so the real
price list becomes a spreadsheet somebody keeps beside it, and the two disagree within a month.
ci/check_no_prices.py fails the build if a price appears in any Python we wrote.
AMOUNTS ARE IN HALALAS and include VAT, because that is what a Saudi customer is quoted: the
shop owner sees 148 and pays 148. amount 14800 is 148.00 SAR.
A BASE AND APPS, NOT FOUR TIERS
A ladder sells the wrong thing. A workshop that wants campaigns and will never look at an
association engine had to buy the engine to reach them, and read the difference between four
columns to find that out. Worse for us: every new thing we build has to be slotted into a
tier, which reprices three plans and re-argues the whole page. Invoicing and CRM are coming,
and the ladder has no room for them that does not disturb what is already sold.
So: ONE base that is the product working, and each app bought on its own. He pays for what he
turned on, the page is a shop rather than a comparison table, and a new app is a row here.
HOW IT ADDS UP, AND WHY IT NEEDS NO NEW CODE. billing-service resolves entitlements across
EVERY live subscription and merges them — its own words: 'per-item catalogue — one
subscription per product — the union IS the entitlement'. Rich limits merge by combining
`limit`, and numbers SUM: the base says feature.campaigns 0, the app says 1, the answer is 1.
Seats add the same way — base 5 plus a seat pack of 10 is 15.
WHICH IS WHY ONLY THE BASE MAY CARRY `messages.monthly`, AND WHY ITS VALUE IS THE WORD
`unlimited` RATHER THAN -1. billing merges its own sentinel by beating every arithmetic;
-1 is just a number to it, and two of them summed to -2 — which refuses every send.
The one-row rule holds for any key carrying the sentinel: it belongs to exactly one row.
AND AN APP IS NOT BOUGHT TWICE, NOR WITHOUT THE BASE. Neither is expressible in billing —
subscribe always creates a row — so both are refused in our own path, operations'
`subscription.activate`, which is the only door the console uses. It decides from the
SUBSCRIPTIONS THEMSELVES (/internal/billing/subscriptions, base-services v0.16.7): a row is a
BASE when it carries `messages.monthly`, which is the one key an app may never repeat. An
earlier `feature.base` flag said the same thing less well — it could not name WHICH
subscription, WHEN it renews or WHAT was paid — and it is gone.
LIMITS ARE THE PRODUCT. The name sells; the limits dict is what actually happens. Three kinds,
and the difference decides who reports the number:
counter  consumed by whoever spends it, reset per period  — messages, custom templates
gauge    the CURRENT value of something owned elsewhere    — seats, branches
boolean  on or off                                          — the apps
AND 0 IS NOT ABSENCE. `0` means the key exists and the answer is DENY — which the console can
render as «هذا تطبيق لم تشترِه بعد، وهذا زر شرائه». A key missing everywhere means NOT
ENTITLED with no reason to show. So THE BASE CARRIES EVERY KEY, including the zeros, and every
shop therefore has an answer for every key whatever else it bought.
AND WE DO NOT SELL MESSAGES. The establishment contracts with Meta directly and Meta bills it
per delivered message, on a card in its own account — we neither buy them nor resell them, so
selling '1,000 a month' was selling what we do not own. Top-up packs went with it.
messages.monthly SURVIVES AS THE SENTINEL, and that is the whole point: unlimited still
counter in billing, so every send is measured and nothing is ever refused for a ceiling of
ours. It is a protection meter — it catches our own runaway loop before the owner's bill does
— and if we ever become a Solution Partner and messages are billed to us, a real number goes
back in this one field and the packs return unchanged.
His actual limit is what WhatsApp allows: 250 unique customers a day before verification,
2,000 after (spec 6.2.2). A second ceiling from us on top of theirs is a number he explains
twice and understands once.

limit_keys.messages.monthly: measured, never sold — see the note above. Uncapped, on the BASE ONLY
limit_keys.staff.seats: people who can sign in; operations owns the count and reports it
limit_keys.branches: branches; operations owns the count and reports it
limit_keys.feature.insights.engine: the association engine (§10.6) — the one thing nobody else has
limit_keys.feature.api: the programmatic link: a till writing visits in the shop's name
limit_keys.templates.custom: templates he writes himself and submits to Meta, per month
limit_keys.feature.base: the base itself — the visit register. Enforced on every write in operations and reminders (core/base_licence.py); a lapsed month keeps reading and stops writing
limit_keys.feature.bookings: the appointment scheduler (docs/وصف-تطبيق-الحجوزات.md) — the staff-side grid, drag-and-drop reschedule, and the booking-to-visit gateway

_removed: feature.roles.custom IS GONE, and its absence is the honest state. It was sold on every tier
and the product has three fixed roles with no screen that creates a fourth — a line on an
invoice for something that does not exist. `ci/check_entitlements.py` found it the moment the
guard stopped counting a price-list LABEL as enforcement. It comes back the day it is built,
as its own app row, and nobody was charged for it in the meantime.

_: THE BASE — the product working. Visits, customers, the service catalogue, visit
confirmation and the reminder that brings people back, the customer's own page, and the
free indicators in «محلّي».
IT CARRIES EVERY KEY, including every app at 0, so no surface anywhere has to tell 'not
bought' apart from 'never heard of it'.
THE TRIAL LIVES HERE, and now it can only live here — there is no higher tier to hand him
for two weeks and take away. He evaluates the product itself; the apps are bought when a
number in his own dashboard makes him want one.
0 MEANS NO TRIAL, and the length is set from our panel by editing this row. No service
knows the number, and a shop that signed up under 14 days keeps 14 whatever we change.
plans.name: الأساس

_: THE APPS. Each grants ONE key and says nothing about anything else — a row that repeated
`staff.seats` would add its number to the base's every time somebody bought it.
ONE PRICE FOR EVERY APP — 99. The first cut derived four different prices from the old
ladder, and the ladder is exactly what we stopped selling: a shop comparing 60 against
200 is reading a tier list again, and asking us to justify why one app costs three of
another.
One number ends that conversation. He reads the sentence about what an app DOES and says
yes or no — which is the decision we want him making, and the only one he can make fast.
AND IT IS EASIER TO SELL THAN TO PRICE. «كل تطبيق بـ99» is repeatable by a partner on a
phone call; four numbers are a page somebody has to open.

_: SAME PRICE AS EVERY OTHER APP — 99. An earlier draft priced this
above the flat rate on the theory that it is the schedule itself rather than an add-on
beside it; that reasoning did not survive contact with the actual decision, which is the
same one number every app in this list sells for. Nothing in this product has ever
shipped at 199 — that figure was a placeholder that outlived the draft it was written in.

_: CAPACITY, NOT AN APP — and the two rows the ladder used to hide. Seats and branches came
bundled with a tier, so a two-branch shop that wanted nothing else had to buy الذكية to
get a second branch.
THESE TWO PRICES ARE THE ONLY ONES NOT DERIVED FROM THE OLD LADDER. They are a starting
point, set here so the shape is complete and reviewable, and they are meant to be argued
with — editing this file is the whole mechanism.
THEY SUM, which is what makes them work at all: buy the seat pack twice and the answer is
the base's 5 plus 20. `quantity` on the subscription would do the same; a repeated
purchase is the simpler story to tell an owner.

_: THE ENTERPRISE SHAPE — priced per conversation, never on the pricing page.
listed=false, so it is invisible to the public list and still subscribable. That is the
whole mechanism: a negotiated customer is moved onto this plan from our panel with an
amount agreed with him, and no code anywhere learns it exists.
IT IS A WHOLE SUBSCRIPTION, NOT AN APP — it carries every key including messages.monthly,
and it is sold INSTEAD of the base rather than beside it. A shop holding both would sum
two message meters into a smaller one, which is why `subscription.activate` refuses it.
The amount here is a PLACEHOLDER, not a price. It is what the plan costs when nobody has
negotiated anything, and the panel overwrites it per subscription.
